newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN's Annan hails planned Mobutu-Kabila meeting.
newsitem.headline: UN's Annan hails planned Mobutu-Kabila meeting.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan, seeking to nail down a planned meeting between Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, said on Wednesday he was gratified they had agreed to talk aboard a South African naval vessel.
"The secretary-general hopes that these talks will set Zaire on a path towards national reconciliation, democracy and prosperity," a statement issued through a U.N. spokesman said.

"The secretary-general is determined to work with the international community to ensure that this change is managed in a concerted and focused manner to avoid further loss of innocent lives," the statement added.

It was prompted by an announcement in Kinshasa by American U.N. Ambassador Bill Richardson that Mobutu and Kabila had agreed to meet on Friday aboard a South African warship as it sailed from Libreville, Gabon, into international waters.

Richardson, acting as a troubleshooter in the Zaire crisis, said after lengthy talks with Mobutu that several African leaders and the joint envoy of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity, Mohamed Sahnoun, would be present for the first direct meeting between the ailing Zairean president and Kabila.
